claim: >-
  The intended private boundary is mostly explicit: no unversioned public
  barrel, production dependency adapter, production package carrier, raw/trusted
  carrier exposure, or duplicate-record behavior is authorized while the named
  decisions remain proposed. However, the implementation guides contain two
  concrete M1 contradictions: they disagree on whether the first qualification
  subject exposes compileCompositionV1 or only an internal normalized-value
  seam, and whether qualification-subject packing is blocked or expressly
  required. Private source-only semantic work is conditionally actionable, but
  the packed M1 qualification boundary is not maintenance-ready.

observedBehavior: >-
  The roadmap's per-phase matrix and self-composition guide expose
  compileCompositionV1 from the M1 qualification subject, while the same roadmap
  says that before both carrier boundaries are accepted the private
  normalized-value seam is the only admitted checkpoint. The current-contract
  guide also says that checkpoint is neither carrier adapter and cannot claim
  trusted-object admission. Separately, roadmap Phase 1 says to stop before
  "subject packing" until public-name, carrier, and both JavaScript-carrier
  authorities exist, then immediately requires two temporary M1 qualification
  archives. OD-004 and the self-composition guide explicitly permit that
  qualification-only packing before ADR-0012.
applicability: >-
  Applies only to private-boundary sequencing and the developer/maintainer
  experience of constructing and qualifying the first private Core subject. It
  does not select a public API, settle carrier semantics, accept a proposal, or
  assess another dispute topic.
benefits:
  - >-
    ADR-0015 gives maintainers a workable private package location without
    weakening publication or runtime-conformance gates.
  - >-
    The current contract enumerates the decisions guarding public naming,
    production dependencies, carrier exposure, and repeated-record behavior.
  - >-
    OD-004 and OD-005 provide narrow qualification-only exceptions, avoiding a
    second throwaway compiler implementation.
  - >-
    Stage0, the own profile, emitter, witness variants, runner, report, and
    attestation surfaces remain private and excluded from the distributed
    archive.
failureModes:
  - >-
    An implementer follows the M1 matrix and embeds proposed trusted-object
    carrier behavior in compileCompositionV1, then overstates an internal
    normalized-semantics result as object-boundary qualification.
  - >-
    Repeated binding records reach an unknown-input entrypoint before ADR-0014,
    but the implementation has no accepted diagnostic or total behavior and
    accidentally selects, merges, or throws.
  - >-
    A maintainer follows the blanket "stop before subject packing" instruction
    and cannot produce the evidence OD-004, ADR-0008, and later roadmap steps
    require.
  - >-
    The governance classifier admits any source under a manifest-valid private
    package. A read-only synthetic invocation with package.json, src/index.ts,
    and raw-decoder.ts returned an empty blocked list. ADR-0015 explicitly leaves
    unresolved-semantic inspection to review, so this is a documented
    manual-review hazard rather than a separate defect.
counterexamples:
  - >-
    OD-004 lines 119-125 expressly permit a private qualification subject to
    pack the proposed carrier before acceptance, contradicting a blanket ban on
    all subject packing.
  - >-
    Roadmap lines 594-600 and current-contract lines 147-159 require a private
    normalized-value checkpoint before carrier acceptance, contradicting an
    unconditional M1 compileCompositionV1 object boundary.
  - >-
    The common API lab declares 30 scenarios and 90 candidate cells, but labels
    itself non-authoritative and measures authoring rather than compiler
    correctness. It cannot resolve the M1 carrier or packaging boundary.

openQuestions:
  - >-
    Is M1 invoked only through an internal normalized-value seam, or through a
    qualification-only compileCompositionV1 carrier wrapper?
  - >-
    If the wrapper is intended, what exact behavior applies to repeated binding
    records and other inputs outside the claimed domain before ADR-0013 and
    ADR-0014 are accepted?
  - >-
    Does "subject packing" at roadmap line 352 mean only production/distribution
    packing, or does it intentionally override the later qualification exception?
  - >-
    Should source-dependency policy mechanically reject premature src/index.ts
    and carrier implementations, or is ADR-0015's manual semantic review
    intentionally the long-term control?
